text:
Leon Draisaitl has 21 goals in 23 games and a 10-game point streak (9 goals, 11 assists), and for now he is doing it on his own line. Mike Babcock split him from Connor McDavid, and the early returns, including a 5-2 win over Florida that Oilersnation wrote up as paying "huge dividends," have kept Edmonton rolling.

Here's the honest part. He's shooting 24% against 19% last season, on 13.8 expected goals, and the Oilers have scored 25.4 more goals than expected with him on the ice. That is a hot streak sitting on top of a great player. The chances are real; the finishing rate almost never holds for a full season. Our range still has him somewhere between 45 and 63 goals, so the cooling we expect still leaves a monster year.

The playmaking is the part people underrate. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 14.5 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 99th percentile among forwards. He's third in the league in wins added by goals this season, which is what a center does when he can beat you as the passer or the shooter.
headline: Draisaitl is scoring at a rate that can't last
